doc.title: Buddy Tate interviewed by Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 3, 1995

title: Herschel Evans and Lester Young's last days
summary: Tate says Herschel never had a bad night, and recalls riding back from Newport with a sick Lester who felt he never made money.

story.theme_name: Lester Young: the man, the sound, the Basie years
story.community_name: Remembering Lester Young: Prez the man and his sound

blocks.x: Well I didn’t think Herschel had a bad night, Herschel Evans. I never thought he had a bad night. Of course Lester declined in his later years from health problems though, with Lester, and I never know what put him on the wrong track because for so many years he was just a health bug. And he was very unhappy with himself the last time we were together we played up to Newport Jazz Festival and he was very sick, he was drinking and drinking. And I rode back with him from Newport and we got lost, which Newport is ordinarily a two hour ride, but we got lost and it was all night. But I’m happy we did, because not knowing it was going to be my last time with him, you know. And he said to me that night he says, “you know I never really made it big.” I said, “what are you talking about?” I ignored him at first, and he said, “did you hear what I said, I said I never really made it.” I said, “what are you talking about” I says, “it’s only two.” I says, “they either play like you or play like Coleman Hawkins.” So I says, “you got more imitators in the entire world.” He says, “all the others are making the money” you know.
